summary.headline: Kross Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32.3% YoY to INR184.3 crore, with EBITDA margin at 12.23% (up 63 bps) and PAT up 24.4% to INR133.12 million.
summary.overview: Kross reported its best-ever Q1 top line, with revenue of INR184.3 crore (up 32.3% YoY) and EBITDA up 39.5% YoY to INR225.54 million. Management attributed growth to volumes across M&HCV, trailers and tractors, and said the extrusion axle beam line is now in production. Steel and conversion-cost pass-throughs are being settled, with the tractor industry already settled from April 1 and CV settlement pending. Management said Q1 is in line with its FY27 targets, though June-July demand is seasonally subdued.

financial_highlights.change: +32.3% YoY vs INR139.3 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue mix: trailers, axles, suspensions and tipping

financial_highlights.change: Management targets 40-45% export growth this FY

segments.name: M&HCV / CV
segments.commentary: Momentum from Q4 FY26 continued into Q1; OEMs indicate a strong September quarter and stronger Q3 and Q4, backed by order books. Tractor-trailer and tipper segments expected to grow well.

segments.name: Trailer axles and suspensions
segments.commentary: Q1 axle volume about 9,500 numbers and suspension volume about 3,200-3,300 (mechanical and air). Volumes up about 30% YoY; management attributes this to Q4 FY26 order spillover and capacity that capped Q4 sales.

segments.name: Tipping jacks
segments.commentary: About 200 kits (management also cited 226 sold in Q1) against 800 per month capacity; management expects 65-70% utilisation by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Tractor
segments.commentary: Demand described as consistent; management expects the tractor contribution to rise meaningfully over coming years.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Existing supply to a European tier 1 is on plan. Four to five product lines are in play; one is in mass production and three are scheduled from H2 FY27. Target of about 8% export share in two years, from about 4-4.5% now.

guidance_outlook: Export growth of 40-45% targeted for FY27.
Export share target of at least 8% of revenue in about two years.
Price increase of about 3-5% on axles from April 1, with a further 1-2% planned in staggered fashion.
Steel settlement at INR4,700 per kg, applied retrospectively, around July 15. Conversion-cost increase still under negotiation with customers.
Seamless tube plant to be commissioned by Q4 FY27, with production trials by end of FY27. Imported piercing mill and other mills are on high seas.
Axle shaft facility using material gathering and press forging technology on track for commissioning by September 2026.
High-pressure mould line for foundry expected in Q3 FY27, doubling foundry capacity.
Management expects margins to expand quarter-on-quarter as pass-throughs flow in.
capex_capacity: Axle beam extrusion line commissioned and in production; volumes ramping.
Tipping jack capacity of 800 numbers per month, with lines set up; 65-70% utilisation targeted by Q4 FY27.
Seamless tube facility: piercing mill received; sizing and straightening mills on high seas; term loan of about INR100 crore taken and to be drawn as machines arrive.
Forging and casting capacity expansion from IPO proceeds is complete; management says no further forging/casting capacity needed for current ramp-up, with utilisation around 70%.
Machining capacity additions continue for new OEM product lines.
demand_pricing: Management says CV volumes will grow well this year, with OEM schedules indicated from September through March; June-July is seasonally subdued due to monsoon.
Trailer-axle growth of about 34% YoY was attributed to Q4 FY26 order spillover and capacity constraints in Q4; management declined to comment on market share.
Prices on the trailer business were raised from April 1. Management says pricing will track competitors, who also face steel inflation.
Management said there was no business loss from the top five customers over the last two years. Top-five share is about 58-59%, versus about 60-63% at DRHP.

Government Parivartan scheme effective October 30, 2026 bars BS4 and older vehicles from Delhi NCR. It offers 10-year road tax holiday, free registration, and roughly 13% discount (5% subsidy plus 8% OEM discount).

qa_highlights.question: How are cost pressures evolving, and have OEM steel and conversion settlements been done?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel settlement of INR4,700 per kg was applied retrospectively around July 15. Tractor industry settled a conversion percentage retrospective from April 1; CV settlement expected soon. Export plans are on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export target and the size of the European tier 1 order?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of at least 8% export share in two years. One product is in mass production; three more start from H2. Export growth of 40-45% is targeted this FY.

qa_highlights.question: Is the trailer-axle growth of about 34% share gain, given single-digit industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was largely Q4 FY26 order spillover. Management declined to comment on market share; capacity expansion should allow further growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst margin quarter behind us, with QoQ expansion ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin expansion. Steel pass-through is retrospective but will come in gradually. Conversion cost increase is the larger factor.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-five customer revenue fall between DRHP and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the top-five share fell from about 60-63% to 58-59% through diversification, and it would check the INR figures.

qa_highlights.question: What are utilisation and debt plans, and does capex need to increase?
qa_highlights.answer: No further forging or casting capex is needed; utilisation is about 70%. No new debt for the existing business. Seamless term loan of about INR100 crore is only partly drawn.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases are planned for axles?
qa_highlights.answer: Axle prices rose about 3-5% from April 1. A further 1-2% is planned, phased to customer acceptance.

risks_watch: Steel and conversion pass-through timing: steel mills may not reflect the retrospective price immediately, and CV conversion settlement is pending.
Competitive pricing: management said pricing tracks competitors, including a larger player in trailer axles.
Seamless tube commissioning slipping past Q4 FY27 and the ramp-up of the high-pressure foundry mould line in Q3.
Ramp-up of tipping jacks (65-70% utilisation by Q4) and whether axle beam volumes build.
Export H2 order inflows from the new tier 1 supplier are still under validation.
Inconsistency on top-five customer revenue: management could not confirm figures on the question about the DRHP versus FY26 numbers and said it would check.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes, capacity and H2 CV demand. Cautious and evasive on market share and the top-five customer question, where it deferred to later checks.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that Kross Limited has concluded its best top line in Q1 FY27 with a sale of INR185.35 crore s, registering a growth of 32% year -on-year, building on the strong momentum of Q4 FY26.
We would not be requiring any more in the forging and casting for these volume ramp -up and we will still be operating at around a 70% utilization.
For our existing business, there is no plan on any debt in the immediate timeline.

adds.what: Seamless tube plant (piercing mill received; sizing and straightening mills on high seas)
Axle shaft facility using material gathering and press forging technology
High-pressure mould line for foundry, doubling foundry capacity
Axle beam extrusion line (commissioned and in production, volumes ramping)

growth.why: Management targets 40-45% export growth in FY27 and at least 8% export share in two years, with the axle beam line live and seamless tube, axle shaft and foundry mould lines due in Q3-Q4 FY27, while OEM order schedules from September support CV volumes; however, no explicit total-revenue FY27 guidance was given and June-July demand is seasonally subdued.
